audit.whatIsWrong: All seven rows disagreed across layers. content win[0..6] read Aurora, Aurora, Aurora, Aurora, LeBlanc, Aurora, Aurora — exactly packet.levelChart — while full phases[N].side read LeBlanc four times then Skill three times. The ratings were also inverted: rows credited to LeBlanc carried 7/10.
audit.why: The content chart matches the kit. Sigil of Malice reaches 700 against Aurora's 900 Q and 825 E, and it is only half a spell until a second ability detonates the 3.5-second mark. Distortion costs 60 to 100 mana, so before 6 LeBlanc cannot both poke and hold the dash. Level 6 is hers because Mimic costs zero mana on a 45-second cooldown and turns a rotation she could not afford into a free one. Aurora's first item takes the lane back. 51.49% over 1342 games fits a lane won everywhere except one level.
audit.corrected: phases[0..3].side = Aurora, phases[4].side = LeBlanc, phases[5..6].side = Aurora, ratings 6/6/6/6/4/6/6, every affected why rewritten in the same proposal. content win[] needed no edit.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 story said 'Mimic doubles whichever spell she casts second' and spikes[2] said her damage 'plateaus without a mythic'.
audit.why: Riot's Mimic text is simply 'LeBlanc casts a mimicked version of one of her basic spells' at 45/35/25 seconds and zero mana. Nothing in the kit supports a doubling rule keyed to cast order, and mythic items are not a current concept. The real spike is that Mimic is free — the mana constraint that held her back through levels 1-5 stops applying to one cast.
audit.corrected: Level 6 restated as a free second cast on a 45-second timer; the first-item spike restated as her needing three cooldowns at once to kill you.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page carried no ability interactions at all — every field was the Aurora template with 'Distortion' pasted in. Four real interactions were absent, and Aurora's E was again called a 'knockback-slow'.
audit.why: enemyKit E is the decisive ability, not W: 925 range (it outranges Aurora's 900 Q), it reveals stealth — which directly answers Across the Veil's invisibility — and 'If the target remains shackled for 1.5 seconds, LeBlanc roots them', so leaving its range inside 1.5 seconds means no root at all. enemyKit Q marks for 3.5 seconds and only detonates when another ability damages the marked target. enemyKit P: below 40% health she goes invisible for 1 second and leaves a Mirror Image that 'deals no damage' for up to 8 seconds. enemyKit W has a 4-second return window. ownerKit E damages and slows, then Aurora hops backward — that backward hop is the shackle-break.
audit.corrected: All four are now on the page: the 1.5-second shackle break as the headline, Chains revealing stealth so W is a range-break not a hide, Sigil being half a spell alone, and the clone as something never to spend a cooldown on.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit in it — 'a four-second return window' is spelled out, and nothing else carried a number.
audit.why: Real values: Ethereal Chains 14/13.25/12.5/11.75/11 at 925 range, Distortion 15 down to 10 with a 4-second return, Sigil of Malice a flat 6 at 700.
audit.corrected: All three now carry digits, with the 1.5-second shackle condition attached to Chains.

audit.whatIsWrong: LeBlanc was called he/his in tldr, tradeGood, tradeBad, ahead, loading, breakdown.wave, dosFull[0].t, dosFull[2].t, phases[0].why, phases[5].why and four report entries.
audit.why: champ-gender.js lists leblanc as female; the owner is 'you', so any third-person pronoun is LeBlanc.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[0] said LeBlanc 'lacks the mana and range to punish your poke before 6'. The range half is false.
audit.why: Ethereal Chains is 925 range — it outranges Aurora's 900 Q. Only Sigil of Malice at 700 is short.

Once her combo is on cooldown, though, you're back in control.

edits.before: With your first item complete you out-trade her cleanly — her damage plateaus without heavy AP stacking, while your combo scales into real burst plus the Between Worlds reset. notes: All seven chart rows disagreed between layers and the ratings were inverted (LeBlanc-sided rows carried 7/10). Fixed the full layer to match content and packet, with paired ratings and rewritten whys in the same proposal. The page named Distortion as the matchup-defining ability everywhere; per the kit it is Ethereal Chains — 925 range against Aurora's 900 Q, revealsStealth (which is the direct counter to Across the Veil's invisibility), and a shackle that only becomes a root if you are still in range after 1.5 seconds. That last detail turns Aurora's W and her E backhop into shackle-breaks rather than escapes, and it had never been stated. Also newly on the page: Sigil of Malice marks for 3.5 seconds and is half a spell until a second ability detonates it, and Mirror Image spawns below 40% health and deals no damage, so no cooldown should ever be spent on the clone. 'Mimic doubles whichever spell she casts second' is not sourceable from Riot's text (which says only that she casts a mimicked version of a basic spell) and was replaced with what is verifiable: zero mana, 45/35/25. whys[0] claimed she lacks the range to punish your poke, which is false against a 925 chain and was actively bad spacing advice. breakdown.cooldowns had no digit ('a four-second return window' is spelled out). Twelve misgendered fields fixed. spikes[2] referenced Riftmaker and 'a mythic'; regrounded on 'your first item' since report[8] prescribes Luden's and mythics are stale terminology. As with the other Aurora matchups, packet.suspectNames flags 'The Weirding's'; the kit file carries no ability names for Aurora so I could not verify it or 'Twin Drift', and avoided both in the rewrites.
